en: XXII. [The Authority and Establishment of the Tantras and Others] Now,
I shall further explain the definitive teaching of the Yoga Tantra.
And the authoritative scripture of the Yoginītantra is being told; listen, O Guhyaka!
And the authoritative standard of the Yoga Tantra is indeed the six parameters (ṣaṭkoṭi).
The Yoginītantra is said to consist of sixteen crores in its extent. 22.2
The Mahāyāna is said to have eighty million distinct sūtras,
as well as fifty million [verses] on the very method of the perfections (pāramitānaya).

The Lord of Munis, possessing the form of the three bodies, has taught all these perfections; the entire teaching of the Sugata, including the Vinaya Piṭaka and all else, as well as the self-teachings of the Śrāvakas. (22.4)
At the conclusion of various offerings, the Bodhisattva taught this great discourse,
the secret of the Yoginī and Yoga Tantras, which is the domain of the Buddhas.
For sentient beings of little merit, there is the teaching that the deities possess a self-nature;
[there is] the visualization of the Dharma, Enjoyment, Emanation, and Great Bliss bodies. (22.6)
The yogin, whose nature consists of wisdom and skillful means, shall swiftly bring about buddhahood. Now,
I shall describe another [teacher], one who has reached the further shore of the ritual procedures for consecration.
One should appoint a preceptor endowed with the characteristics previously described;
for the purpose of consecrating fashioned images and the like made of refined materials, one should purify the ground.
The consecration of the ground, beautified by canopies, banners,
and flags.
One should place an image of the Earth Goddess, or a complete statue, or a book, or a cloth painting, before oneself. 22.9.
Having worshipped the maṇḍala-cakra situated in space with the five offerings, one should recite three times: "Thou art the pledge; I am the pledge. || 22.10 ||
One should recite [this] with offerings, just as all the perfectly awakened ones are currently established in Tuṣita.
Just as it was enjoyed by Queen Māyā, so let them remain here in this form.

O Protectors, being constantly present here, please accept these flowers and other offerings for the sake of [the person named] so-and-so, for the purpose of increasing the thought of awakening (bodhicitta).
Having thus addressed the Tathāgatas with this, the wise one should offer praise; he should perform the immersion three times and cause the vessel to revolve along with the water.
One should bathe [the image] with fragrant scented oil and with bark.
Furthermore, one should always bathe the image with each individual water-pot.
One should bathe [the deity]; subsequently, one should cause the Blessed One, who resides in space, to enter into the maṇḍala, the wheel, the images, and so forth. || 22.15 ||
[The word] *ākāśasthaṃ* [is the correct reading], whereas *ākāsthaṃ* is in manuscript A;
[the word] *maṇḍala* [is the correct reading];
[the word] *praveśayet* [is the correct reading], whereas *praveśayat* is in manuscript A.
Whatever task is to be performed by the ten actions, such as legal proceedings and so forth,
one should open one's eyes and remain in the midst of the vajra-eye.
One should open [the eyes]; likewise, flowers, incense, lamps, perfumes, and food offerings—after those, one should complete all rites by means of the fire-offering (homa). || 22.17 ||
The wise one should cause all the gods, who have Agni as their mouth, to be installed; once the characteristics for installation are attained, he should perform this ritual of praise. 22.18.
One should worship [the deity] as one pleases when there is a sound like that of many drums.
The gift of food brings courtesy and the satisfaction of people; it is nourishing. || 22.19 ||

Through Puṣṭi one gains nourishment and the good fortune of people; through Māṅgalyā, peace; and through Śāntikā, the pacification of various sufferings, calamities, and the like, as well as the rite of Dūṣaṇa-yāga.
O Lord, since it is impossible to establish that which is non-abiding, the request of the disciple should be fulfilled together with [the teacher] for the sake of merit. (22.21)
The request [to teach] is by way of non-conceptual form; the installation of the deity is its stabilization by way of that same form.
And when the deities and world-protectors remain eternally, then,
O Lord, the world shall abide, endowed with both the worshipful and the unworthy.
Thus ends the twenty-second chapter, the ritual procedure for the consecration of deities.
